teams.heading: Maro Itoje rejects French clubs with new Saracens deal, England future secured
teams.body: Maro Itoje has agreed a new Saracens deal, rejecting Top 14 interest that had been mooted for Perpignan and Bordeaux. His current contract, signed in 2024, was due to expire after next year's World Cup. The 31-year-old, who has 102 caps, was rested for England's summer Tests after showing signs of fatigue. “He is staying,” Venter said of Itoje. The Guardian says the extension will enable him to continue his international career.

lead.why: A new, fan-relevant England story about Itoje's future, with a national-team link, and it is not a pundit piece or a women's or club-only item.

teams.heading: Galthié recalls Alldritt, drops Depoortere and names Ward as training partner
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has recalled Grégory Alldritt to the 42-man squad for the November Nations Championship, dropping Bordeaux Bègles centre Nicolas Depoortere to make room for former Junior Springbok Jeremy Ward. Ward, a 30-year-old Stade Français midfielder, is not eligible for France until 2027 under World Rugby's residency rules, so he is named as a "training partner" only. The squad is built around injury gaps, with Thomas Ramos ruled out of all four matches and Matthieu Jalibert, Emmanuel Meafou and Julien Marchand also absent.

lead.why: The 42-man squad is the day's biggest France story, with Alldritt's recall, Depoortere's omission and an uncapped South African in the group.

teams.heading: Farrell names uncapped Ulster pair McNabney and Benson in Ireland squad
teams.body: Andy Farrell has called up two uncapped Ulster players, James McNabney and Jamie Benson, for the November window, with Jack Conan ruled out by a shoulder injury. McNabney, 23, is back from an ACL injury that cost him the entire 2025/26 season. Benson joined Ulster from Harlequins this summer and has played centre and out-half this season. Farrell said: "It's always great to give people a chance for the first time." Dan Sheehan captains the 36-man squad in Caelan Doris's absence.

lead.why: Two uncapped Ulster players joining the senior squad is the freshest men's national-team news and the one fans will talk about.

teams.heading: Tommaso Menoncello likely to miss Italy's autumn Tests with shoulder sprain
teams.body: Italy's Tommaso Menoncello is likely to miss the autumn Nations Championship games after a left shoulder sprain, suffered when he went off in the 43rd minute of Toulouse's 43-40 Champions Cup win over Exeter Chiefs on Sunday. The injury is expected to keep the centre out for several weeks. Named Six Nations Player of the Championship in 2024, he is a major loss for Gonzalo Quesada, whose side lost all three summer games against Japan, New Zealand and Australia and face South Africa first.

lead.why: A new injury to a named Italy centre, with a clear impact on the autumn Nations Championship, is the story a fan would text a mate about.

teams.heading: Scotland women: Aicha Sutcliffe makes first start against Australia in Canberra
teams.body: Scotland women's interim head coach Dave Butcher has handed hooker Aicha Sutcliffe her first Scotland start, one of three changes for the final WXV Global Series match against Australia in Canberra. Sutcliffe has six caps off the bench, and the Glasgow Warriors hooker comes in as Scotland chase a first win in this WXV campaign after a 56-12 defeat in Sydney. Sarah Bonar returns in the second row after missing that loss through illness.

lead.why: The men's items are already-reported Glasgow and Tuipulotu stories or an off-field honours story, so this fresh Scotland women's selection is the strongest new item in the pack.

teams.heading: Tandy reveals Tommy Reffell suffered knee injury as he defends squad calls
teams.body: Steve Tandy has revealed that Tommy Reffell, one of the Nations Championship omissions, suffered a knee injury. The head coach, who has now named four squads, says the flak is part of the job: "I cop flak wherever I go, that's something I'm getting used to." Tandy also said he had a few tough phone calls to make, insisting that he would rather players know where they sit. The 39-man group opens its November programme against Japan in Cardiff.

teams.heading: Argentina are eighth of 12 after a 28-28 draw with Australia
teams.body: Argentina's most recent result was a 28-28 draw with Australia, and the log now has them on three played, one won, none drawn and two lost. Across those three matches they have scored 97 points and conceded 99, a points difference of -2. The next fixture is against Ireland. Their best-ever world ranking is No. 3, reached in 2007–08.

teams.heading: Will Genia says Wallabies struggled to match All Blacks' skill and tempo
teams.body: Former Wallaby Will Genia says Australia's current style left them exposed in the Bledisloe Cup, which New Zealand won 2-0 with wins in Auckland and Sydney. On the I Love Rugby podcast, the 110-cap scrum-half said the Wallabies are not yet at the level of either physicality or skill to impose themselves on the All Blacks, and that New Zealand's tempo and pace made them hard to stick with. Les Kiss is trying a different style, Genia noted, but the 19-50 and 21-43 defeats show the gap.

lead.why: It is a new item that gives a fan a clear view on why the Wallabies lost the Bledisloe Cup, and it is the only fresh candidate about the men's side.

teams.heading: Yuka Kanematsu's Japan women's sevens complete Asia series double over China
teams.body: Japan's women's sevens completed a double in the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series, beating China 14-7 in the Colombo final to win Leg 2 and the series title. The Sakura Sevens finished with the maximum 40 series points, having also beaten China 24-7 in the Suzhou final in August. Five players in the Colombo squad earned their first caps, and the team now turn their attention to the HSBC SVNS in Dubai.

teams.heading: John Kirwan hails All Blacks' depth after Jordie Barrett's late withdrawal
teams.body: Sir John Kirwan says Australia did not press the All Blacks as South Africa did during the Springboks series, but believes Dave Rennie can take real positives from the 50-19 and 43-21 Bledisloe wins. The depth was the point: Jordie Barrett's late withdrawal forced a change in the centres, Quinn Tupaea went off early, and the replacements stepped up. Kirwan singled out Scott Barrett. "The team is getting better, and that is the most important thing," he said on the Rivals Rugby podcast.

lead.why: The newest item on the shortlist, and it frames the Bledisloe wins around the All Blacks' depth, with Kirwan's view clearly attributed.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield expects Springboks to play more expansive rugby on end-of-year tour
teams.body: Victor Matfield expects the Springboks to show a more expansive side on the end-of-year tour, with more of attack coach Tony Brown coming in. Speaking on the Rugby Rivals podcast, the former Bok captain said the side reverted to their physical, pressure-based DNA after the opening defeat to the All Blacks in the Rivalry series, and that the expansive part of their game still needs growing. He expects Rassie Erasmus to give young players a chance, but warned against wholesale changes.

lead.why: A new Springbok story about how the national side may play in November, with the opinion clearly attributed to Victor Matfield, and it has not been run before.
